title: Introduce profile reconciliation and impact-aware release synthesizer
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a profile reconciliation step to onboarding and a release synthesizer that produces impact-ranked release notes for model variants. Includes migration for existing manifests and an opt-in flag for release automation.
body:
Context: As model onboarding scaled to dozens of variants we've observed drift between per-variant performance metadata and the canonical model manifest. This drift made changelogs noisy and caused regressions in production rollouts because release notes did not accurately represent quality or cost impact. This PR introduces two pieces: (1) a profile reconciliation pipeline that merges per-variant profiles into a reconciled canonical profile with provenance and a deterministic fingerprint, and (2) an impact-aware release synthesizer that converts profile deltas into structured, ranked release notes and suggested rollout policies.

What this PR does: Adds a new manifest v2 schema field set (AffordanceSignatures, SLOTargets, CostEstimateTokens, ProfileFingerprint). Implements a reconciliation worker that ingests variant profiles, canonicalizes metric names, applies decay-weighted aggregation for rolling baselines, and emits a reconciled profile plus a delta bundle. The release synthesizer consumes delta bundles and outputs a human-readable release summary and a machine tag set for the console. It also groups changes by semantic impact (quality, latency, cost, API) and scores them to prioritize notes.

Implementation highlights: - manifest/v2: added optional fields with backward-compatible parsing (old manifests remain valid). - reconciliation/worker: Go service with a compact pipeline (fetch -> normalize -> aggregate -> sign -> emit). Aggregation uses median-of-means and time-decay to be robust to outliers. - release/synthesizer: Python tool that maps deltas to note templates, ranks by impact score, and links Linear tickets heuristically (search by model alias, tag, and recent commits). - CLI hook: onboard-cli now exposes `onboard reconcile --dry-run` and `onboard synth-release --delta <bundle>` for maintainers. - DB migration: lightweight migration to add profile_fingerprint index for query performance.

Files changed (high level): listed below. Small illustrative snippets included inline for the manifest change.

Example manifest diff snippet:
@@
- "profiles": [ { "name": "default", "metrics": { "ppl": 12.3 } } ]
+ "profiles": [ { "name": "default", "metrics": { "ppl": 12.3 }, "affordance_signatures": ["summarization:high", "instruction-following:medium"], "slo_targets": {"latency_ms": 150, "p95_latency_ms": 320}, "profile_fingerprint": "sha256:9f8b..." } ]
@@

Commits: - "init: add reconciliation worker, manifest v2 parser and tests" - "cli: onboard reconcile/synth commands and docs" - "synth: impact scoring, note templates, linear-link heuristics" - "db: add profile_fingerprint index and migration" - "tests: add integration tests for reconcile + synth end-to-end"

Changed files (representative): - redwood-model-registry/onboard/manifest_v2.go (new fields + parser) - redwood-model-registry/onboard/reconcile/worker.go - redwood-model-registry/onboard/reconcile/aggregate.go - redwood-model-registry/onboard/reconcile/provenance.go - redwood-model-registry/onboard/cli/reconcile_cmd.go - redwood-model-registry/release/synth/synth.py - redwood-model-registry/release/synth/templates.md - redwood-model-registry/db/migrations/20260212_add_profile_fingerprint.sql - redwood-model-registry/tests/integration/test_reconcile_synth.py - docs/model_onboard/reconcile.md - docs/release_notes/impact_scoring.md - .github/workflows/reconcile-ci.yml - tools/onboard-cli/main.go - tools/onboard-cli/README.md

Review conversation (high level): - Aaron Patel: "Can we guarantee deterministic fingerprints if profiles arrive out-of-order? Also please add a short note on how decay windows are chosen." - Maya Chen (author): "Fingerprint is computed from normalized, sorted key tuples and timestamp-agnostic aggregates; added a unit test for out-of-order arrivals and a short rationale in docs." - Leah Thompson: "Impact score seems subjective; can we expose config for weights and tie it to an offline evaluation?" - Maya Chen: "Exposed weights in synth config and added an offline evaluation harness (tests/perf) — results are in the PR artifacts." - Diego Ramos: "DB migration looks safe but let's add a roll-forward script for on-prem installers." - Maya Chen: "Added migration safety wrapper and an installer hook. Marked the migration as idempotent." - Leah Thompson: "CI showed perf bench failure initially — was that addressed?" - Maya Chen: "Yes, transient benchmark flakiness was caused by a shared GPU on the test host; we isolated the job and re-ran. All checks green now."

CI checks and status: - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests: pass - lint: pass - docs-check: pass - release-notes-validator: pass - perf-bench: fail (first run, flaky) -> re-run -> pass - reconcile-ci (new workflow): pass

Testing & validation: - Added deterministic unit tests for fingerprinting and normalization. - Added integration test that runs reconcile -> synth -> validates note templates against expected anchors. - Manual smoke runs on staging with two real model bundles (bert-lite variants) verified that synthesized notes matched reviewer expectations and correctly suggested canary rollout policies.

Migration and rollout plan: - Step 1 (opt-in): enable manifest v2 and reconciliation for a single team for 2 weeks, monitor profile drift and note quality. - Step 2 (wider opt-in): add a console toggle for auto-synth release notes, default off. - Step 3 (auto): after 30 days and successful metrics, flip default for new onboarding flows. All migrations are idempotent; rollbacks remove the profile_fingerprint index and keep legacy profile fields intact.

Related work: ENG-3421 (onboard stability), ENG-3498 (release automation), SUP-712 (customer ticket: release notes missing variant cost deltas).

Merge details: Merged with squash by Leah Thompson. Merge commit: sha256:3b7a2f1e9a8c4f5d2e1b9c1a6b2e3f9c5d6a7b8c

Notes for maintainers: - The synth scoring config lives in release/synth/config.yaml and is adjustable without code changes. - Backwards compatibility: old manifests are readable; new fields are optional. - If you see unexpected fingerprints, run `onboard reconcile --recompute --project <id>` to regenerate.
